problem: Existing audio-visual navigation (AVN) methods treat binaural audio as undifferentiated input, ignoring left/right spatial disparity, and use static or pre-defined audio-visual fusion that cannot adapt across environments.
motivation: Sound sources may be occluded or in reverberant spaces where vision cannot reveal the source, so the agent must infer direction from inter-channel differences. The relative usefulness of vision vs. audio also varies with the environment, so fusion should be adaptive.
key_idea: Add a Stereo-Aware Attention Module (bidirectional cross-attention between left/right audio feature channels) to the audio encoder, and fuse audio and vision with an audio-queried attention plus a learned sigmoid gate (AGDF), trained end-to-end with PPO.
insight: Both modules give gains that are partly complementary. In the ablation (Table 3), removing SAM sharply hurts SPL/SNA (e.g. Matterport3D-Same SNA 34.3 to 20.9), while removing AGDF mainly hurts SR. The ablation numbers are somewhat inconsistent, though: in the audio-only Table 2 the single-module variants sometimes beat the full model, and the full-model rows in Table 3 differ from Table 1.
method: Feature extraction: two independent 3-conv (8x8, 4x4, 3x3) + FC CNN encoders for visual (128x128 RGB or depth) and binaural audio spectrograms (65x65x2 Log-Mel or 65x26x2 STFT), producing 512-d features.

Stereo-Aware Attention Module (SAM): after the audio CNN, the 64-channel feature map is split into left and right halves, bidirectional scaled dot-product cross-attention is applied (Q_L attends K_R,V_R and vice versa), followed by a 1x1 conv projection, a residual connection and concatenation.
AGDF attention: the SAM-processed audio feature (embedded to 768-d) is the Query and the concatenated audio-visual feature is Key/Value in multi-head attention, giving f'_av.
AGDF gating: w = sigmoid(f'_av W'_av + f_a W_a + b); K_f = w*f'_av + (1-w)*f_a, adaptively weighting the cross-modal enhanced feature against audio.

Policy learning: a GRU over the fused features feeds an Actor-Critic head trained with PPO and GAE; the reward is +10 for a correct Stop, -0.01 per step, +1 or a negative reward for reducing or increasing geodesic distance; the discrete actions are Forward/Left/Right/Stop with a 500-step limit.

setting.backbone: Small CNN encoders + SAM + AGDF + GRU actor-critic (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces AudioGoal episodes on Replica (9/4/5 scenes train/val/test) and Matterport3D (73/11/18 sound-category split); no extra data
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB or depth (128x128) + binaural audio spectrograms
setting.action_space: Discrete: Move Forward, Turn Left, Turn Right, Stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (geodesic distance used only in the training reward)

numbers.extra: 78 training sound categories; unseen scenes, seen sounds

numbers_note: The paper does not specify the exact split name (it says unseen scenes); 'test' is assumed. Table 3 ablation full-model numbers differ from Tables 1-2 and are not listed. Only depth input results are shown.
results: AGSA beats AV-NaV, SAVi, Direction Follower and Frontier Waypoints on Replica and Matterport3D in both heard and unheard settings (e.g. MP3D unheard SR 36.5 vs 33.5, SPL 26.2 vs 21.9 for AV-NaV). In the audio-only Replica-Multiple setting, SPL is 63.2 vs 44.9 for AV-NaV (about 40% relative gain).
limitations: Unheard-sound gains are modest (Replica unheard SR 48.3 vs 47.3), and absolute unheard performance stays low.
Baselines are limited and dated (AV-NaV, SAVi, etc.); ablation and audio-only tables are inconsistent and single-module variants sometimes beat the full model.
Evaluated only in simulation, with no real-robot tests and no multi-seed statistics.
